title: Malicious service creation and PowerShell execution on WORKSTATION6
summary: An unknown service PGUJLOAKFQFVOMHGFQPX was installed on WORKSTATION6 by pgustavo immediately after a network logon from 172.18.39.5. The service executes an encoded PowerShell command that disables script block logging and AMSI, downloads code from http://10.10.10.5, and runs it -- classic ransomware/wiper behavior. A network connection on port 445 was also observed just before service installation.
evidence: Service PGUJLOAKFQFVOMHGFQPX installed by pgustavo at 06:57:48.992 on WORKSTATION6
Service command line uses PowerShell -enc (encoded command) to bypass defenses
Decoded PowerShell disables Script Block Logging and AMSI, downloads from http://10.10.10.5, runs downloaded code
Network connection from 172.18.39.5 to 172.18.39.6:445 observed at 06:57:48.982 just before service install
IP 172.18.39.5 rated internal but logon followed by suspicious service creation
User pgustavo is Domain (lab) user with normal host WORKSTATION5, unexpected activity on WORKSTATION6

recommended_actions.action: Terminate the PGUJLOAKFQFVOMHGFQPX service and associated PowerShell processes
Reset credentials for pgustavo account and audit for lateral movement
Block http://10.10.10.5 at perimeter and investigate source IP 172.18.39.5 for compromise
Full malware scan of WORKSTATION6 with updated definitions

title: Encoded PowerShell execution with defense evasion on WORKSTATION6
summary: On WORKSTATION6, SYSTEM launched an encoded PowerShell command via cmd.exe (parent: services.exe) that decoded to disabling script block logging, bypassing AMSI, and downloading malicious code from external IP 10.10.10.5 (not in company network). This follows the prior ALERT-001 malicious service creation on the same host, indicating an attack chain.
evidence: Encoded PowerShell command -enc flag detected on WORKSTATION6 at 06:57:49
Decoded command disables ScriptBlockLogging and bypasses AMSI (bypass_amsi: true, disables_script_block_logging: true)
Command contacts external IP 10.10.10.5 (suspicious: private address not in company network ranges)
Process chain: services.exe → cmd.exe → powershell.exe → whoami.exe
Rule tags confirmed: T1059.001 (PowerShell), T1027 (Obfuscated Files)
Prior ALERT-001 on same host involved malicious service creation and PowerShell execution
related_to_prior: ALERT-001 on WORKSTATION6 - malicious service creation leading to this encoded PowerShell execution, indicating coordinated attack chain

recommended_actions.action: Block outbound connections to IP 10.10.10.5 at firewall/proxy
Investigate services.exe parent process from ALERT-001 for malicious service creation
Restore ScriptBlockLogging settings if modified by the encoded command
Scan WORKSTATION6 with full antivirus/EDR scan for downloaded payload

title: C2 Beacon via Encoded PowerShell on WORKSTATION6

This continues the attack chain from prior alerts ALERT-001 and ALERT-002 on the same host.
evidence: powershell.exe ran as SYSTEM with -enc flag, parent was cmd.exe
decoded command disables Script Block Logging and AMSI, downloads from web, contains nested base64
IP 10.10.10.5 flagged as suspicious, private address not in company network ranges
whoami.exe executed by powershell confirming reconnaissance
process chain: services.exe -> cmd.exe -> powershell.exe -> whoami.exe
rule tag T1071.001 confirms C2 over HTTP/S
related_to_prior: Continuation of attack chain from ALERT-001 (malicious service creation) and ALERT-002 (encoded PowerShell with defense evasion) on WORKSTATION6

title: Azure Guest Agent lsass access - Likely legitimate infrastructure activity
summary: CollectGuestLogs.exe, a legitimate Microsoft Azure Guest Agent component (v2.7.41491.993), opened lsass.exe with memory-read access. The process chain shows WaAppAgent.exe → CollectGuestLogs.exe → conhost.exe → cmd.exe, all running as SYSTEM, which is normal Azure infrastructure behavior. The file path, version, and parent process all match the official Azure Guest Agent distribution.
evidence: CollectGuestLogs.exe is a legitimate Azure Guest Agent component at C:\WindowsAzure\GuestAgent_2.7.41491.993_2020-09-17_150914\CollectGuestLogs.exe
Process chain: WaAppAgent.exe (parent) → CollectGuestLogs.exe → conhost.exe → cmd.exe, all as SYSTEM user
Command line: 'CollectGuestLogs.exe -Mode:ga -FileName:C:\WindowsAzure\CollectGuestLogsTemp\73d22eaa-ee60-4181-b12d-9037b2b2c176.zip'
Alert timed 2 seconds after process start, consistent with agent initialization
Rule tag T1003.001 matched but legitimate software can trigger credential access detections

recommended_actions.action: No immediate containment required - verify this is the legitimate Azure Guest Agent on this workstation
Confirm Azure Guest Agent is expected/approved on this host per organizational policy
